intro: Tuatapere is a small town in western Southland, near the south coast of New Zealand's South Island and the edge of Fiordland. Inland from it, off Lillburn Monowai Road, a nature walk leads into dense, wet forest of moss and ferns. A reader sent us the great totara that stands on that walk, a single column of peeling grey and red-brown bark, and puts it at about a thousand years old.

trees.story:
A reader sent this totara from the totara trees nature walk off Lillburn Monowai Road, in the Southland hills inland from Tuatapere, with a GPS fix taken at its foot. They named it Podocarpus hallii, Hall's totara, and gave it an age of about a thousand years and a girth of 831 centimetres.

The photograph looks up the trunk from its root plate. A single column rises out of the moss, far wider than a person could reach round, its bark grey and red-brown and peeling in long vertical strips, with cushions of moss climbing it. The trunk runs straight out of the top of the frame. Around it the forest is dense, wet and green, with ferns, mossy branches and smaller trees pressing in.

The age and the girth are the reader's figures, and no register we hold lists the tree, so read them as theirs. The stringy bark fits a totara, but the photograph does not settle which of the two totaras it is, so this page names the genus and gives the reader's species beside it. If you know more about it, tell us here.

Follow the walk into the forest and look for the widest trunk on it.
